answer: Trust can spiral outward from a seed grove of verified agents: each round, every agent splits its trust score evenly among peers it has actually transacted with, and propagation stops after about log(n) rounds. A Sybil cluster touches the honest graph through only a few attack edges, so little trust leaks in however many fake accounts it mints. Like a falcon needing a real perch, the attacker must earn costly genuine relationships with honest agents to gain any weight.
